Approximation methods, such as solving the linear Laplacian system Lx = b, remain computationally expensive for large graphs, despite optimizations reducing the time to 𝑂˜ (𝑚) [12, 21, 61]. Random projection-based methods [76– 78] allow approximate BD queries in 𝑂 (log 𝑛) time but require 𝑂˜ (𝑚/𝜖 2 ) time in preprocessing, involving large-scale matrices impractical for massive networks or scenarios where only a limited set of node pairs are of interest. Additionally, these methods assume full graph knowledge, which is often unrealistic in practice. To address these issues, Liu et al. [42] proposed novel algorithms that only require local information and can efficiently answer BD queries for a set of node pairs, without the need for costly preprocessing.
